waypoints.name: North Fork Sauk River Trailhead
waypoints.note: Coordinate and elevation as published by the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest for the Trinity Trailhead, where Buck Creek Trail #1513 and Chiwawa River Trail #1550 enter the Glacier Peak Wilderness. The North Fork Sauk River trailhead is 20.2 mi away on a different approach: both of this route's approach waypoints — Buck Creek Pass at 9.5 mi and the Cool/Gerdine Basin camp above it — are reached from Trinity, and the route's own itinerary begins 'Trailhead to Buck Creek Pass, 12 mi'.

itinerary.cal: Buck Creek Pass access depends on Suiattle River / Trinity-area road status, which has had washout issues in recent years — confirm current road conditions before relying on this trailhead.

waypoints.name: North Fork Sauk Trailhead (FR-49, Sloan Creek Road)
waypoints.note: Road-end trailhead on Sloan Creek Road (FR-49). The White Chuck and Suiattle roads are closed, so this is the open way in: North Fork Sauk Trail #649 climbs to the PCT, then north over Red Pass to the Kennedy Ridge junction and Glacier Creek.

waypoints.name: Kennedy Ridge Trail / PCT junction
waypoints.note: Kennedy Ridge Trail meets the PCT about a quarter mile north of Kennedy Creek; turn to follow the PCT toward Glacier Creek.

waypoints.name: Glacier Creek PCT crossing camp
waypoints.note: Good established campsites with reliable creek water about 2 miles along the PCT from the Kennedy Ridge junction.

waypoints.name: Ridge saddle above camp
waypoints.note: Climb SSE up the basin from the Glacier Creek camp to this flat saddle where the route gains the open slopes below Kennedy Glacier.

waypoints.name: Vista-Kennedy saddle
waypoints.note: Saddle between Vista Ridge and the Kennedy Glacier icefall; rope up for glacier travel from here.

waypoints.name: Kennedy Glacier crevasse band
waypoints.note: Deep, dramatic crevasses form on this small, steep glacier; parties often hug the left wall under Kennedy Peak to dodge crevasses at the cost of added rockfall exposure.

before.descent_text: Reverse the ascent line — the correct SE-ridge descent is generally easier to pick out looking downhill than it was on the way up, and most parties who wandered onto the harder Class 4 rock on the ascent spot the easier Class 3 bypass ('sidewalk' ledge) on the way down. From the true summit, downclimb the short (~100 vertical foot) summit block via its broken south-side terrain rather than traversing climber's-left, which dead-ends above the exposed south face in sustained 4th-class ground. Continue down the scree/talus climber's-left of the SE ridge crest back to the Foggy Lake outlet on the same cairned line used on the ascent, then retrace the maintained Gothic Basin trail — through the basin meadows, the steep timbered switchback band, and the Weeden Creek ford — back to the Barlow Pass trailhead. This is a walk-off/downclimb descent with no rappelling required in normal summer conditions. The real hazards are loose rock and fall exposure on the summit block and upper scree, and, in early-season or wet/icy conditions, hard snow on the slabs and snowfield just below the ridge, where an ice axe (and caution on the creek crossing) is warranted. A short handline is occasionally carried by conservative parties for the final summit-block downclimb, but it is not standard gear for this route.

before.approach: Drive the Mountain Loop Highway from Darrington (WA-530) roughly 17-19.7 miles, then turn onto Forest Road 49 (Sloan Creek Road) and continue about 6.6-6.7 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead (2,070 ft, vault toilet, no potable water). Hike the North Fork Sauk Trail #649 through old-growth forest, passing Red Creek camp (3.5 mi) and Mackinaw Shelter (5 mi), then climbing roughly 3,000 ft over the final miles to the Pacific Crest Trail junction (~8.2 mi from the trailhead). Follow the PCT north about 0.7 mi to White Pass, then continue about 2 more miles on the PCT to Indian Pass (~4,962-5,000 ft), the low point/junction with the Indian Creek Trail and the jumping-off point for the peak. Total one-way approach to Indian Pass is roughly 10.9-11 miles.
